expectations.text: Identifies agentpool and/or kubernetes.azure.com/agentpool as CAST AI reserved labels whose values are overwritten
expectations.evidence: answer.md section 1: '`agentpool` (and its successor `kubernetes.azure.com/agentpool`) are on CAST AI's **reserved labels** list' and quotes the official docs verbatim: 'If you configure any of these in a Node Template, Cast AI will overwrite your values with the ones it determines... Verified against live https://docs.cast.ai/docs/autoscaler-reference-node-labels-and-taints: the AKS table lists both keys and the page carries exactly this reserved-labels warning.

expectations.text: Explains that AKS requires every node to carry a pool identity label, which is why CAST AI stamps its own value and cannot honor custom ones
expectations.evidence: answer.md section 1: 'On AKS every node must carry a pool identity — that is how AKS tracks node pool membership — so CAST AI cannot remove, rename, or delegate this label, and no Node Template value for it will ever survive. This is an AKS platform requirement, not something a template can opt out of.' Also cites the docs' AKS entry: 'Set to `castai` for Cast AI provisioned nodes. Required by AKS for node pool membership.'

expectations.text: Does NOT claim that a node template can set a custom agentpool value or that CAST nodes can join a customer-named Azure agent pool

expectations.text: Gives the supported alternative: one node template per pool, targeted with the scheduling.cast.ai/node-template label (and/or template custom labels)

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT claim that a node template can set a custom agentpool value or that CAST nodes can join a customer-named Azure agent pool
suggestions.reason: Negative assertions are weakly discriminating in a free-form answer — a vacuous one-line reply would also 'pass' it. Consider pairing it with a positive check that the answer explicitly refutes the misconception (e.g., 'The answer explicitly states that setting the label in a node template has no effect / is overwritten'), which this run's answer does satisfy ('setting agentpool in a node template silently does nothing').

No assertion guards against a subtler hallucination class: an answer could claim a PodMutation or webhook can rewrite the agentpool label ON THE NODE (or on Azure pool membership) rather than only rewriting pod selectors. An assertion like 'Does not suggest any mechanism that changes the node-level agentpool label value to a customer-chosen string' would discriminate between correct and confidently wrong outputs; this run passes such a check (Sec. 1: 'CAST AI cannot remove, rename, or delegate this label').
